item.title: La Liga midfielder laments failed Barcelona transfer: ‘It was a dream for me’
item.description: La Liga midfielder laments failed Barcelona transfer: ‘It was a dream for me’ Speaking on Radio MARCA , Racing Santander midfielder Andre Almeida has revealed that Barcelona made an attempt to sign him when he was still at Valencia, only for the club to block the transfer. The 26-year-old Portuguese star is currently on loan at Racing from Valencia for the season, having joined the club last summer. However, if things had turned out differently, he could have become a Barcelona player a few years ago. Almeida claims Barcelona wanted him During the interview, Almeida revealed that Barcelona tried to sign him shortly after he had joined Valencia. The midfielder himself was intent on making the transfer happen, as he saw it as a ‘dream’, but Los Che blocked the move as they were battling relegation at the time. Almeida is currently on loan at Racing Santander. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) “No, no, it was in January, in my first season there, as we were fighting against relegation and I was an important player, and I’d also just arrived at Valencia,” he said. “They wouldn’t let me leave, but obviously it was a dream for me. But you have to accept it when you sign contracts and the club has taken that decision, and I have to accept it.” Almeida signed for Valencia in the summer of 2022, arriving from Vitoria Guimaraes in a deal worth around €8 million. So, going by the player’s statements, the attempt from Barcelona would have come during the January transfer window of 2023, when Xavi Hernandez was in charge of the team. Almeida saw the chance to join Barcelona as a dream. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) However, Valencia proceeded to not sanction the midfielder’s sale as they were fighting for survival in La Liga under former manager Gennaro Gattuso. How has Andre Almeida’s career progressed since then? Having failed to secure his dream move to Barcelona, Almeida remained a regular at Valencia and has gone on to make 119 appearances for the club, registering four goals and 13 assists. Capable of playing in multiple positions, the 26-year-old Portuguese ace moved to Racing Santander on loan in the summer transfer window, where he has played six matches so far. The midfielder was not a part of the Racing Santander squad that lost 7-2 to Barcelona in La Liga earlier this season.

item.title: Thierry Henry stunned by ‘joke’ Jude Bellingham performance as Real Madrid blow Liga title race wide open with Clasico win
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Barcelona forward Thierry Henry has heaped praise on Real Madrid following their vital 2-1 El Clasico victory over his old club. The Frenchman was particularly blown away by Jude Bellingham's performance, describing the England international's dominant display in midfield as an absolute joke. Henry praises compact Real Madrid Henry has admitted he was highly impressed by Madrid's tactical setup during their crucial 2-1 El Clasico victory over his former club Barca. Speaking after the weekend's blockbuster fixture, the Frenchman noted that the vital win marked the first time this year he had seen Madrid play in such a compact and resilient manner. According to Henry, Los Blancos were incredibly difficult to beat on the day, conceding very few clear opportunities while remaining highly dangerous on the counter-attack. Despite his natural allegiance to Blaugrana, Henry was quick to acknowledge the impressive nature of the complete performance from the capital club. Bellingham performance was a joke While Kylian Mbappe grabbed the headlines with two goals and the official Man of the Match award, Henry reserved special praise for England international Bellingham. The former Arsenal striker was left entirely in awe of the dynamic midfielder's all-around contribution to the vital victory. Speaking to Betway , Henry explained just how highly he rated the phenomenal individual display. "It was the first time this year that I’ve seen Real Madrid playing like that," Henry noted. "They were compact, not conceding a lot of opportunities, being very difficult to beat and sound on the counter. "Kylian Mbappe scored two goals and was named Man of the Match, but Jude Bellingham? Wow. The way he played reminded me of England’s game in Mexico. He was holding it, turning people, winning a foul, finding a pass or going through himself. I have to give him a lot of credit, the way he played was just a joke." Mourinho answers his critics The vital victory also served as a major statement for manager Mourinho, who had faced external pressure heading into the massive fixture. Henry noted that the jury had been out on whether the renowned coach could still deliver on the biggest stage, but this result firmly proved his enduring tactical qualities. "Well done to Mourinho," Henry added. "The jury was out on whether he could still do it, and he showed he can. They knew they couldn’t afford to lose because a gap of nine points with that goal difference would have been very difficult. “It’s still a long road, everyone thought it would be very difficult to stop Barcelona, but this is why it’s very difficult to predict these things. item.title: Nuggets' Aaron Gordon warns Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg that league will humble him
item.description: Nuggets' Aaron Gordon warns Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg that league will humble him originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It has been clear from the get-go that Yaxel Lendeborg was going to play a big part in the Golden State Warriors ' success. During the preseason, head coach Steve Kerr was already talking about how critical he would be to the offense. Lendeborg has taken the reins of the offense when Steph Curry is out or on the bench, but at one point, he was surprised by the opportunity. “Well, it's very shocking to hear it now. But I mean, I get the point. The two other guys are hurt. Jimmy was one of the main scorers on this team. So, going to have to try to fill in his role until he gets back. And I've been in positions where I've had to score the ball a lot, I guess, or an extra amount that I would like. I feel like I'll be able to step into that role for sure. Just got to continue to work at it, get the confidence to do that. But I mean, I feel like everything's going to be trending up the right way," Lendeborg said. The rookie has already faced off against one of the best players in the league, Luka Doncic. Lendeborg made it clear that he lost respect for Doncic after their first NBA matchup. During a recent sit-down with Denver Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon, the NBA champion offered Lendeborg some advice, warning the rookie phenom that the league would humble him. “As far as like your NBA journey, just stay with it. There's some freaks in this League you know what I mean? Like real monsters in this League. This sht will humble you. I thought I was the #1 option in Orlando, not really. Got to Denver, took a couple of steps back, won a championship, improved my game now. Know this League is going to humble you, just always bring that sht, what you learned from, like your mom's, what you learned from the job, bring that, bring that. That's why the Warriors picked you,” Gordon said. Lendeborg is a mature rookie, so when he has a game in which a superstar gets the best of him, he isn't going to let it bother him. Instead, he can use that experience as motivation to improve. The forward has been a great addition for the Warriors, and there is no sign of him slowing down. Gordon's advice was valuable, reminding Lendeborg that he needs to be ready for the challenges that come with playing in the NBA. item.title: Sacramento Kings source shares whether Doug Christie will now be fired after 0-5 start
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images The Sacramento Kings have had a dreadful start to the new season, losing each of their first five games. It was always going to be a difficult start for the Kings because of the absence of several key players, but such a poor start has led to calls from many fans for a change of head coach. However, Doug Christie’s seat is set to be safe, for now. Sacramento Kings to stick with Doug Christie despite 0-5 start Even before the Sacramento Kings’ 12-point defeat to the New Orleans Pelicans, there were rumours that Christie’s job was at risk. Many felt the latest loss was the last step and he would be shown the door, especially with fans on social media calling for him to be fired. However, a Kings team source has reportedly told The Athletic that Christie is set to remain in charge and there is no immediate threat to his future. The report claims that ‘there is an internal belief that Christie deserves a fair chance to be evaluated with a team that is much healthier than this current Kings lot’. Ben Simmons, Keegan Murray, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell are all currently injured. Simmons has, in fact, been ruled out for the season due to an Achilles tendon tear. The stance on Christie’s future may yet change if the Kings continue losing games at the same rate, but as things stand, there are no plans to part ways with him. Sacramento have two tough games coming up, first against the unbeaten Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday and then against the Dallas Mavericks on Monday. It remains to be seen if the Kings’ stance on Christie will remain the same if they end up losing both of those games. item.title: Patrick Kane Learned How Detroit Still Feels About Him
item.description: Before the Chicago Blackhawks and the Detroit Red Wings dropped the puck Thursday night at Little Caesars Arena, Patrick Kane’s son, Trick, and Alex DeBrincat’s son, Archie, sounded the horn to start the game . Those two families have been close for quite some time. DeBrincat played with Kane in Chicago from 2017-2022 and he also played with him in Detroit from 2023-2026. Kane signed a two-year contract with the Blackhawks in July, and Thursday was the first time he had been back in Detroit since. Oct 29, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Chicago Blackhawks defenseman Artyom Levshunov (55) takes a shot defended by Detroit Red Wings right wing Alex DeBrincat (93) in the first period at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Patrick Kane received a standing ovation from Detroit Red Wings fans in the first period After the first media timeout of the opening period, the Red Wings played a tribute video of Kane’s three seasons in Detroit on the arena video board. Fans stood and gave him an ovation, players on both teams tapped their sticks on the ice, and Kane skated out and saluted the crowd. The tribute came hours after interim general manager Shawn Horcoff announced that forward Dylan Larkin had been suspended without pay, after Larkin’s agent told the team he would not report to the rink. 88❤️ pic.twitter.com/H3LspwqWLM — Detroit Red Wings (@DetroitRedWings) October 30, 2026 Alex DeBrincat comments on Kane returning DeBrincat talked about Kane’s return after the game, in comments published by Red Wings team reporter Jonathan Mills . “It’s always good to see him. I think he was a big part of our team for a couple years there. It sucks that he’s not here anymore, but he’s such a good player. It’s good to see him back in that uniform if he’s not going to be here, so it’s always fun to play against him…He’s a great player.” Detroit won the game 4-1, so the Red Wings got the result and Kane got the reception. DeBrincat and Kane were teammates in two cities, their sons are friends, and the video tribute showed Detroit has not forgotten what Kane did here.

item.title: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta stands by Max Dowman frustration after cup red card
item.description: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has voiced his opinion on the Max Dowman situation -Credit:DARREN STAPLES, AFP via Getty Images Mikel Arteta has revealed that he remains "very disappointed" that Max Dowman was sent off against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday. The Gunners suffered a stunning penalty shootout defeat to the Fishermen in the Carabao Cup after the match ended 1-1 following regulation time. Summer arrival Bruno Guimarães was the player who missed a vital penalty, with Jay Lynch diving low and hard to his left to pull off the save. Conor Haughey then finished calmly to seal the shootout 5-3 in Fleetwood's favor, as the League Two club progressed to the quarter-finals. There, they will face Everton on December 15. However, it wasn't only the shocking result that grabbed attention, with Dowman's red card late in the contest sending soccer fans into a frenzy. With just four minutes left, the 16-year-old was tackled by Harrison Neal on the byline, the Fleetwood defender catching Dowman's leg in the process. Thierry Henry addresses Ballon d'Or criticism after Lamine Yamal and Kate Scott remarks Wayne Rooney launches into furious foul-mouthed rant at Manchester United players -Credit:Carl Recine, Getty Images The teenager responded immediately by lashing out at Neal, triggering a confrontation among players. Referee Michael Salisbury then reacted by showing a red card to Dowman, with Arteta visibly furious at the call, as per The Mirror . And now, the Spaniard has reinforced his criticism of the official. Speaking during his pre-Liverpool press conference on Friday, he said: "Very disappointed, to be fair, especially with the reckless tackle that he received. "His reaction is minimal in compared to the action. It is what it is, we have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Max's action is clear, obviously we have a very different opinion, you have to read into the context, the age, the player. It could have been really bad and we're really lucky today that he doesn't have a broken foot." Addressing his heated response toward Dowman, Arteta continued: "My reaction comes in a moment of heat and extreme frustration because I know the consequences of that, especially for Max. We discussed it just before we went out and it will continue happen unfortunately because of how he attracts opponents. "He's 16 and we have to be very protective of him but also very straight with what we expect from him towards the team, individual and the clubs." Via @BrianCoz pic.twitter.com/pjF8Jx7cph - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 30, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Breece Hall, New York Jets We never expected Hall to play last week, but there is a real chance he suits up this week. However, it could be risky for his long-term health if he hasn't been able to get in a full practice yet. Everyone saw what happened with Saquon Barkley last week after rushing back from a soft tissue injury. Like hamstrings, a quad injury can be tricky and is prone to re-aggravation. item.title: Arteta warns Dowman 'we are not in Disneyland' after red card
item.description: Mikel Arteta had words with Max Dowman after the teenager was sent off [Getty Images] Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has told Max Dowman "we are not in Disneyland" and that he intends to hold the teenager to the same standards as other first-team players. Dowman, 16, was sent off in the 85th minute of Arsenal's penalty shoot-out loss to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after reacting to a heavy challenge by Harrison Neal and will serve a three-match ban . A visibly annoyed Arteta spoke to Dowman as the teenager left the pitch, and on Friday spoke about the incident for the first time, saying he warned the attacker before the game about dealing with provocation. "I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out," Arteta said of his words to Dowman. "But, I don't know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say 'I don't like the reaction'. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am." Arteta revealed that he had spoken to Dowman on Thursday and said there were "no issues at all" between the pair. However, he added that he needs to be "very straight" with Dowman and clear of the standards expected. Dowman was sent off for the England U19s earlier this month where he was also on the end of heavy challenges in a match with the United States. Of that red card, Arteta said: "They are his age. They are 16 – the same. What is the reaction? That is the level and that is the reaction. "And whether it is right or wrong, that is the reaction." Arteta also spoke of the impact the red card had on the team, saying: "And the reaction when I don't win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time. "So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level. "We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. "But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair." The Gunners did appeal against the red card but the Football Association (FA) upheld the decision. Of that, Arteta said he was "very disappointed", adding "we are lucky today that he (Dowman) hasn't had a broken foot." item.title: Youri Tielemans explains why Man United squad wants Michael Carrick to stay
item.description: Youri Tielemans explains why Man United squad wants Michael Carrick to stay Manchester United midfielder Youri Tielemans has explained why the squad want Michael Carrick to continue at Old Trafford. The English manager is under severe pressure after a run of two wins in 12 games across all competitions this season. The poor form has seen the team drop down to 16th in the Premier League table after eight games. The Red Devils have already exited the EFL Cup and have lost two of their three games in the Champions League. The situation has added to speculation over Carrick’s future, with several candidates mentioned as his possible replacement. However, the Belgian midfielder, who joined United from Aston Villa this summer, has thrown his weight behind the English manager. Carrick’s role in Tielemans’ Old Trafford move Speaking to TNT Sports , Tielemans explained why the United squad want Carrick to continue at the Theatre of Dreams. The Belgian said: “I came here partly because of him, because he wanted me here. He wanted me to help the team out.” “So I’m very happy for him to stay, and the whole group, we don’t want a sudden change. We don’t want a big change that is going to disrupt things more than they are. We just need stability, we need to keep working hard, and it’s going to turn at some point.” Tielemans went on to insist that the entire squad is backing the English manager, adding: “Since I’ve come in, he’s always done his work. He’s tried to put a system in place that we all feel comfortable in. I joined this summer, because he convinced me to come over and help the team out.” “I can only speak positively about him, and everyone in the changing room would do the same. item.description: Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark announces he will step down in January originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormack will be stepping down from his role in January 2027. ESPN's Pete Thamel announced the news Friday. He is leaving to pursue a career outside of college sports. “When I accepted this job, my goal was to put this conference on an upward trajectory and truly believe that the future of the conference could not be in better shape,” Yormack said. “The next commissioner of this league will inherit a conference that is ’16 Strong.’ There has never been a better time to be a member of the Big 12 than right now.” Yormack took the reins as Big 12 commissioner in 2022, shortly after Texas and Oklahoma packed their bags for the SEC. He succeeded Bob Bowlsby and helped the conference land a new TV deal with Fox and ESPN. "I think in all fairness, had he not joined us and convinced us to go early on redoing our television deal, we all believe we could have ended up like the Pac-12 did," Kansas Chancellor and Big 12 Board Chair Doug Girod said about Yormack, per ESPN . "We certainly recognized that and believed it at the time. As it played out, it demonstrated it was the right move. His leadership, experience and networking in the media world have continued to be extremely beneficial for us." Yormack led the way through a major conference realignment, welcoming eight new schools. He took advantage of the PAC-12 divorce by adding Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah. “I am looking forward to passing the baton to the next commissioner and continuing to cheer this league on as a lifelong fan of the Big 12,” Yormack told On3’s Brett McMurphy. The Big 12 extended Yormack’s contract through the 2030 college football season, according to ESPN . “When I accepted this job, my goal was to put this conference on an upward trajectory and truly believe that the future of the conference could not be in better shape,” said Yormark. “The next commissioner of this league will inherit a conference that is ’16 Strong.’ There has never been a better time to be a member of the Big 12 than right now.” In his four years as commissioner, Yormack did things the untraditional way by landing deals with companies like Monster Energy Drinks and other sponsorship and marketing agreements. Girod said Yormack was everything the Big 12 was looking for because he was not a traditional athletic director but was innovative and aggressive in bettering the conference. item.title: Wrestling legends loved Christian Watson’s WWE-style return to Packers-Panthers
item.description: What Christian Watson pulled off in the Week 8 game between the Green Bay Packers and Carolina Panthers was nothing short of a WWE -like storyline. Watson exited the contest in the second quarter with a chest injury and was even forced to make a trip to the hospital for further testing on his injury. At that point, we thought Watson’s night was over because who could possibly expect the Packers wideout to return to a game after all of that. However, we were dead wrong, as Watson came back to the stadium one quarter later, and not only did he return to the contest, he received a target immediately. MORE: NFL trade deadline tracker – Grades for every deal, list of available players If you’ve watched professional wrestling over the years, you’ve seen plenty of ambulance entrances and exits, so Watson’s return had a very WWE-style feel to it. Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) WWE legend and Hall of Famer Triple H shared his reaction to Watson emerging from the ambulance to return to the game. The only thing missing, Triple H said, was entrance music. “This isn’t a video game… you did that!!! Next time we’ll work on getting you some entrance music,” Triple H said when getting wind of Watson’s postgame comments about his return. Fellow WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman revealed that the origin of the ambulance entrance was in 1991 in WCW, when the now-defunct company did something similar with Sting. MORE: Josh Jacobs assigns blame for ‘handcuff’ TD celebration And, we’re not clear if he’s joking, but Heyman said football is “pre-determined.” “We did this with (Sting) in 1991 in WCW (vs Ravishing Rick Rude), and the industry has repeated it with great success in numerous circumstances,” Heyman said. “My most sincere compliments to the (NFL) creative team. Nicely Done… I love football. Even though it’s pre-determined,” Heyman added. Christian Watson sees WWE parallel Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson (9) reacts after making a catch against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field. Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) After the game, even Watson admitted he felt like he was in a scene from a WWE show. “I used to watch WWE as a kid,” Watson said. However, everything checked out, which allowed him to make his epic return to the field. Watson finished the game with eight receptions for 113 yards, with two of those catches and 13 of those yards coming after his return. (Defensive coordinator) Brian (Flores) is doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. […] I’ve got a lot of respect for this team, the way they play, but we’re looking forward to this; this will be good.” Let’s take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will earn a victory over the Vikings in this week’s Honolulu Blueprint. "This was so important for our self-awareness ahead of the coming season. Because before this, Dortmund became Bundesliga champions and the cup final that we lost 5-2," Lahm concluded. item.title: Iraola glad to raise Liverpool fans' hopes but says hard work ahead
item.description: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola (Paul Currie) Andoni Iraola is pleased his side's performances have left some Liverpool fans dreaming of a Premier League title challenge ahead of Sunday's match at home to champions Arsenal, even if it is too soon for him to pay much attention to the table. Victory at Anfield would see Liverpool move to within three points of Arsenal, who are currently level at the top of the table with leaders Manchester City. Liverpool are on a five-game winning run in all competitions, a sure sign of their progress as they adapt to the methods of former Bournemouth manager Iraola in his first season on Merseyside since replacing the sacked Arne Slot. But Iraola said Friday: "It is still October. We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we've played against each other once so halfway through the season. That's when you can start to look at the standings. "Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better." But asked if he welcomed the increasingly buoyant mood among Liverpool fans, the Spaniard replied: "For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win." Arsenal moved level with City at the top of the table following a 2-0 win over Everton last weekend, but then suffered a huge upset defeat on Tuesday after being knocked out of the League Cup on penalties by fourth-tier Fleetwood. "We know Arsenal and how good they are," Iraola said. "They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge. "It's going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday. I hope we will be at a level to win this game." As for Liverpool's recent run, a cautious Iraola said: "It is five wins (in a row) but just two are in the league so if we are talking about the league we still need more wins to recover points. "But definitely we know what we want in terms of we have to improve a lot of things. But, if you can do this process while you are getting results, it is always nice." jdg/nf

item.title: Osi Umenyiora on the journey that led to NFL Africa
item.description: Born in London and spending his formative years in Nigeria, Osi Umenyiora had never even heard of American football until he moved to the U.S. as a teenager. After moving to Auburn, Alabama, he took up the sport in high school and eventually earned an opportunity at Troy University. He was drafted by the New York Giants in 2003 and went on to win Super Bowls XLII and XLVI. Umenyiora spent ten years with the Giants and two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before retiring in 2015. The rest, as they say, is history. Yet Umenyiora's story was far from over. "My whole story has just been one of pure fortune, and so I looked at it like, 'Okay, I've been given this opportunity, and now I'm working with the NFL. How can I now give this opportunity to more people?'" That's where an e-mail to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell snowballed into NFL Africa, the league's initiative to grow the game on the continent and perhaps Umenyiora's most impactful chapter yet. In the conversation below, part of NBC Sports' By Way of Africa series , Umenyiora reflects on his childhood in Nigeria, the story behind NFL Africa's creation, and what the initiative's growth means to him. *This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Mary Omatiga: Osi, you were born in London, but I read that you lived in Nigeria from age 7 to 14. What memories come to mind when you think of your childhood there? Osi Umenyiora: Nigeria to me is a very special place. It's a place that I hope to one day return to and live. Growing up there meant so much to me. My family being there, coming back there. Because of the way we were raised — and we were raised in a very Nigerian way — when I got there, the only difference really was the climate. Other than that, it was basically the same things going on. But overall, it was just a really, really great experience and time in my life. It's something that I'll never forget and something that I cherish. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora How did that time there shape you into who you are today? Umenyiora: In a multitude of ways. The environment there teaches you how to survive first and foremost. It instills toughness. There are so many things that you see there that, whenever you leave that environment, the ability to thrive in those situations, you can carry them with you pretty much anywhere. I know they say that if you can make it in New York, you can make it anywhere, but really, it's if you can make it in Lagos, Nigeria, you can pretty much make it anywhere. item.title: Nicolas Jackson and the celebration that reveals his Premier League revenge mission
item.description: The first thing to say about Nicolas Jackson is he seems, generally, a nice enough person and I have no reason to think otherwise. The second is that his current goal celebration is perhaps the most terrifying thing in the Premier League right now: the finger raised first to the ear, the outstretched thumb hovering in the balance and then flicking downwards, followed by the action of slicing his throat from left to right and the cold stare down the lens of the pitchside camera and into your soul. Mercy? No, very much like Russell Crowe’s Maximus in Gladiator , itself the inspiration behind the striker’s thumb down gesture, Nicolas Jackson is out for vengeance, and his targets are in his sights. Jackson has scored seven goals for Aston Villa since joining from Chelsea at the end of August. His double in Villa’s 2-1 win over Manchester City, and his former manager Enzo Maresca, last weekend, to end their 100 per cent record , took him to six goals in his last six appearances for Unai Emery ’s side, including four in four in the Premier League. He has become the leading man in the new-look attack that is Emery’s Villa 2.0, ensuring the departure of Ollie Watkins, who Villa sold to Al Hilal for £50m, has largely gone forgotten. He is doing everything Emery wants from his striker: pressing from the front, running the channels, and, yes, being clinical in the box when the chances arrive. goodnight, villans pic.twitter.com/YT46ScjsEo — Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) September 19, 2026 That it comes as a surprise that Jackson has suddenly found an eye for goal is perhaps unfair, but it is a reputation that was forged, of course, by his previous two-year spell in the Premier League at Chelsea. Jackson was 22 when he was signed by the ensemble of Chelsea’s various sporting directors for £32m, as part of a transfer policy designed to bet on youth and potential. He arrived as a relative novice, following a season at Villarreal where he had played less than half of the minutes available to him at LaLiga. Scoring 17 goals in 44 appearances under Mauricio Pochettino in his first season in English football was, on reflection, a decent return, but Jackson became defined more by the opportunities he didn’t take than the ones he did. Rightly or wrongly, a narrative set in: Jackson was willing but raw, wasteful and, at times, ill-disciplined (managing to pick up eight yellow cards before Christmas in his first season is some achievement, but it added to the frustration). After Chelsea sacked Pochettino that summer the pattern continued under Maresca, scoring 10 goals from 12.3 xG.
